vocab.text: Notice the pair: a reputation can be true or false, but a stereotype is almost always too simple. The way to test both is the same: wander, and talk to a local.

paras: Ask ten people who have never been to Naples, and nine will tell you the same thing: it is dirty, it is dangerous, and you should only stay one night on your way to the Amalfi Coast. It is a reputation that the city has had for more than a hundred years, and it is the reason many travelers never get out of the train station. The ones who do stay often say the same sentence when they come home: nobody told me.

What surprises visitors is not the monuments, which are many, but the street life. Naples is a city where people still live on the sidewalk: grandmothers who talk from one balcony to another, men who play cards outside the bar, and small shops that have belonged to the same family for four generations. The streets are crowded and loud, and the traffic is a show of its own. But the city has a warmth which is hard to find in places that are cleaner and more organized. The stereotype is not completely false. It is just the smallest part of the story.

Scenario 1
Tell a colleague about a city that surprised you. Describe one person you met, one place where you ate, and one thing which was different from what you expected.
Scenario 2
A supplier from abroad is visiting São Paulo for two days. Recommend a neighborhood where he should stay and a restaurant that only locals know.
Scenario 3
Describe the city where you grew up to someone who has never been there. What is the stereotype, and what is the truth?

items.situation: A colleague asks about the best place you have ever traveled to.
tips: It is a city that... / It is the place where...
Give one detail that nobody expects.

items.situation: A visitor asks you where to eat in São Paulo, like a local.
tips: Say who goes there: people who...

items.situation: Someone says a city you love is dangerous and dirty.
tips: Describe one neighborhood where the reality is different.

items.situation: Describe a person who helped you on a trip.
tips: He was a man who... / She was the woman who...

items.situation: Recommend a hidden gem in the city where you live.

answerkey.title: Reveal the model answers
list: We met a taxi driver who told us about the city.
We ate at a small restaurant which had no menu.
This is the street where Giulia grew up.
Naples is a city that surprises everybody.
answerkey.note: Who is for people, which is for things, and where is for places. That works for people and things, and it is the most common in conversation. The relative word replaces the second he, it or there, so do not repeat them.

listenings.text: Hi Felipe, it's Laura from the events team, with the details for the Milan trade fair. The hotel that we booked is ten minutes from the fair, so you can walk. The colleague who organizes our stand is Paolo, and he will meet you at the hotel on Monday morning. The fair finishes on Friday at noon. You told me you wanted to stay for the weekend, so I found a train which leaves Milan at two and arrives in Naples at a quarter to seven. If you prefer Florence, which is closer, let me know before Wednesday.

Felipe, it's Giulia. Laura told me you are going to Naples, and I am so happy, because it's the city where I grew up. Please don't listen to people who say it is dangerous. Three things. First, stay in the old center, which is where the life is. Second, there is a small pizzeria near my grandmother's street that has no menu. You sit down and they bring you the pizza that they made that day. Third, on Sunday, take the funicular, which is a little train that goes up the hill. The view of the bay from there is breathtaking. Send me a photo.

extra_audio.text: First, Giulia asks Felipe how his weekend in Naples was. Then Felipe says it was the city that surprised him most. After that, he describes the neighborhood where they stayed. Next, he talks about a taxi driver who told them the history of the city. Finally, Giulia says the pizzeria they found is a hidden gem.
